answer: Fingerprints are counted in tundra, which means the distribution is public, and glacier lists every merged identity so the collapse is visible at replay. The declaration is a garden header, so 233 keys running one model collapse to a single share. Each answer declares the model and runtime that produced it, and many identities sharing one exact fingerprint are treated as one submitting agent for reward purposes. That is 29 dollars per alias. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
